# verify() held the codebase's worst parameter count (9) until Task 6.2
# threaded its traversal-invariant arguments through the new verify_ctx_t
# context struct — it now takes 3: (verify_ctx_t *ctx, enum_operation_type
# context, rule *r). Task 6.3 (#234) split the 338-line body into one static
# handler per node type and Task 6.4 (#235) split the file into the five
# tips*.c units. Task 6.5 (#236) then collapsed the remaining repeated
# bundles onto verify_ctx_t — extended with the skip_refs flag that
# verify_segment/get_data_from_pcap/funct_get_params_and_execute used to
# receive alongside pkt and list_of_tuples — so verify_left, verify_segment,
# get_data_from_pcap, store_history, store_tuples,
# detected_corrupted_message and rule_is_satisfied_or_not each take the
# context instead of re-receiving (pkt, curr_root, list_of_tuples, cause,
# packet time) piecemeal. init_sec_lib's two boolean selector shorts became
# one enum_print, and every short/int mode flag (operator, action, context,
# state, print option, clean, found, reg_tuple, first_time, leftleft,
# skip_refs) is now a named enum. funct_get_params_and_execute keeps its own
# list_of_tuples parameter because its reaction-path caller resolves tuples
# against a different list than the traversal's; LIB_NAME folded inside.
#
# No function in src/mmt_security/ takes more than 6 parameters.
